issues.summary: As a user, I want to log in to the VWO dashboard with valid credentials so that I can access my account and dashboard
issues.description:
Source: App VWO Login API doc + HLR (Login).

POST https://app.vwo.com/login with {"username", "password", "remember", "recaptcha_response_field"}. Content-Type: application/json. No auth header.

Acceptance Criteria:
- POST /login with valid username+password returns 200/2xx
- Response includes user object: id, name, email, accountId
- Response includes account/policy flags (isActive, policy.ruleset)
- Response includes currentAccount.planType and productsEnabled
- User is redirected/able to access the dashboard
- Content-Type: application/json accepted; malformed body returns 4xx

issues.summary: As a user, I want to see a clear error when logging in with invalid credentials so that I know my login failed
issues.description:
Source: App VWO Login API doc + HLR (Login).

Invalid email/password must return an error (no dashboard access).

Acceptance Criteria:
- POST /login with wrong password returns 401/error status
- POST /login with unknown email returns error
- Error response contains a meaningful message/code
- No session/token issued on failure
- Empty/missing username or password fields rejected with 4xx

issues.summary: As an API consumer, I want the login response schema validated so that integrations receive consistent, documented data
issues.description:
Source: App VWO Login API doc (Response - Validation).

Response JSON contract includes: id, name, email, accountId, isDemoAccount, shouldSeeOnboarding, isPasswordSet, isAccountVerified, policy {id, name, ruleset}, accounts[], currentAccount {id, timezone, isTrial, daysRemaining, isExpired, productsEnabled, planType, accountStatus, dataLocation}, isActive, createdOn, lastLogin, imageUrl, appVersion, twoFactorAuthenticationMethod, isSamlEnabled, proxyToken, playerToken.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Response matches documented JSON schema field-for-field
- policy.ruleset exposes canBrowse, canDesign, canPublish, isAdmin, isOwner booleans
- accounts[] present with id, name, isMainAccount, isAgencyAccount, isLinkedAccount
- currentAccount includes planType, productsEnabled (testing/deploy/data360), daysRemaining
- proxyToken and playerToken present on successful login
- Schema documented and versioned for API consumers

issues.summary: As a user, I want session and token handling (proxyToken, playerToken, cookies) so that I stay authenticated across API calls
issues.description:
Source: App VWO Login API doc (proxyToken, playerToken) + HLR verification dimensions (Auth, Cookie, Token).

Acceptance Criteria:
- Successful login returns proxyToken and playerToken
- Tokens are usable for subsequent authenticated API requests
- Session cookie (if any) is set and honored
- Remember flag persists session when true
- Token expiry/refresh behavior defined and handled
- Tokens are not logged or exposed in plaintext logs

issues.summary: As a user, I want to register/sign up so that I can create a new VWO account
issues.description:
Source: HLR (Registration section).

Registration API is the second API family in the HLR. Verification dimensions: URL, Payload, HTTP Method, Status, Request body, Response body, Header, Auth, Cookie, Token.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Registration endpoint is documented with URL and HTTP method
- Valid registration payload creates a new account
- Response body returns account/user details on success
- Duplicate/registered email returns an error
- Invalid/missing fields rejected with 4xx
- Header, Auth, Cookie, and Token behavior verified and documented

issues.summary: As a QA engineer, I want an API test matrix for login and registration covering headers, auth, cookies, and tokens so that API quality is verified
issues.description:
Source: HLR verification dimensions (URL, Payload, HTTP Method, Status, Request body, Response body, Header, Auth, Cookie, Token).

Acceptance Criteria:
- Test matrix exists for Login API covering all verification dimensions
- Test matrix exists for Registration API covering all verification dimensions
- Each row maps to a test case with expected status
- Header variations (Content-Type, User-Agent, Referer) covered

issues.summary: Login API returns 500 instead of 401 for invalid credentials
issues.description:
Source: App VWO Login API doc + HLR (Login invalid credentials path).

POST /login with a wrong password should return 401/error status, but the service returns HTTP 500 with a generic server error, hiding the auth failure.

Steps to reproduce:
- POST https://app.vwo.com/login with {"username": "valid@user.com", "password": "wrong"}
- Observe HTTP 500 instead of 401

Expected:
- HTTP 401/4xx with a meaningful error message/code
- No session/token issued on failure

Acceptance Criteria:
- Invalid credentials return 401 (not 500)
- Error response contains a message/code
- No proxyToken/playerToken issued on failure
- Regression test added for the invalid-password path

issues.summary: Session cookie not honored on subsequent authenticated API requests
issues.description:
Source: App VWO Login API doc (session/token handling) + HLR verification dimension Cookie.

After a successful login, the session cookie set by the login response is not sent on subsequent API calls, so the user appears logged out on the next request.

Steps to reproduce:
- Login successfully and capture Set-Cookie
- Call an authenticated endpoint with the cookie
- Endpoint returns 401/session expired

Expected:
- Session cookie persists and is honored across requests
- Remember flag persists session when true

Acceptance Criteria:
- Cookie round-trip works for authenticated calls
- Token/session state consistent after refresh
- Test matrix (HLR Cookie dimension) covers this

issues.summary: proxyToken and playerToken missing from login success response
issues.description:
Source: App VWO Login API doc (Response - Validation: proxyToken, playerToken).

The login response contract requires proxyToken and playerToken on successful login, but the live response omits them, breaking clients that depend on the documented schema.

Steps to reproduce:
- POST /login with valid credentials
- Inspect response JSON for proxyToken/playerToken
- Fields are absent

Expected:
- Response matches documented JSON schema field-for-field
- proxyToken and playerToken present on successful login

Acceptance Criteria:
- Response schema validated against documented contract
- proxyToken and playerToken present
- Schema regression test added

issues.summary: Duplicate registration email returns 200 instead of a conflict error
issues.description:
Source: HLR (Registration section, duplicate email case).

Registering with an already-registered email should return an error/conflict status, but the API returns 200 with a success body, allowing duplicate accounts.

Steps to reproduce:
- Register a new email (201/success)
- Register the same email again
- Observe 200 instead of a conflict/4xx error

Expected:
- Duplicate/registered email returns an error
- No duplicate account created

Acceptance Criteria:
- Duplicate email rejected with meaningful status
- No duplicate account record created
- Regression test for duplicate email

issues.summary: A/B test variations not distributed evenly under high traffic
issues.description:
Source: PRD 4.1 Experimentation & Testing, FR1; traffic splitting for A/B campaigns.

Traffic split across A/B variations is heavily skewed under load (e.g. 80/20 instead of 50/50), producing biased experiment results.

Steps to reproduce:
- Create an A/B campaign with 2 variations (50/50 split)
- Drive high traffic through the experiment
- Observe variation distribution diverges from configured split

Expected:
- Traffic split deterministically and evenly per configured weights
- Results remain statistically valid

Acceptance Criteria:
- Distribution matches configured split within tolerance
- SmartStats conclusion is trustworthy
- Load test covers split accuracy

issues.summary: SmartStats confidence metric incorrect for small sample sizes
issues.description:
Source: PRD 4.1 SmartStats Bayesian engine; FR2 (Must); risk: data accuracy.

SmartStats reports high confidence (e.g. 99%) for variations with very small sample sizes, misleading users into declaring a winner prematurely.

Steps to reproduce:
- Run a campaign with low traffic (few conversions)
- Open the SmartStats report
- Observe overstated confidence/probability

Expected:
- Confidence metrics remain valid under low sample sizes
- Report explains actionable conclusion (winner / keep running / inconclusive)

Acceptance Criteria:
- Small-sample guardrails in place
- Confidence reflects uncertainty correctly
- Cross-tool validation matches

issues.summary: Session recordings stop after 30 seconds on long pages

issues.summary: Implement Secure User Login and Authentication for VWO Application
issues.description:
As a VWO user,I want to securely authenticate into the VWO application using my supported authentication method,so that I can access my VWO account and its authorized functionality.

The login experience must provide secure, reliable, and user-friendly authentication while preventing unauthorized access.

Application: app.vwo.com

Login entry point: app.vwo.com/#/login

VWO's current authentication documentation identifies these supported login methods: Email/Password, Google, SSO, and Passkey. Forgot Password and Remember Me are also part of the authentication experience.





The system shall provide a login page that allows an existing VWO user to authenticate.

The login page shall provide the applicable authentication options:

Email address

Password

Sign In

Remember Me

Forgot Password

Sign in with Google

Sign in using SSO

Sign in with Passkey

Availability of Google, SSO, and Passkey may depend on account configuration, device, browser, or organization configuration.



A registered user with valid credentials shall be able to authenticate successfully using email address and password.

Upon successful authentication, the user shall be taken to the VWO account/dashboard.



If the user enters invalid authentication credentials, the system shall reject the authentication attempt and shall not grant access to the VWO account.

The system shall provide appropriate feedback to the user.



The system shall validate required login information before attempting authentication.

An authentication request shall not be successfully submitted when required information is missing.



The user shall be able to initiate password recovery using Forgot Password.

The documented flow is:



      ↓

Enter registered email

      ↓

Reset Password

      ↓

Receive password-reset email

      ↓

Open reset link

      ↓

Enter new password

      ↓

Confirm password

      ↓

Reset password

      ↓

Login with new password

VWO documents this password-reset flow for existing accounts. 



The user shall be able to select Remember Me during login.

When selected, VWO documents that the session can be extended up to 14 days on the same browser and device. Without Remember Me, the default documented session expiration is 2 hours of inactivity. 



Where the user's account supports Google authentication, the user shall be able to select Sign in with Google and authenticate using the registered Google account. 



Where SSO is configured for the organization, the user shall be able to select Sign in using SSO.

The user shall be redirected to the organization's configured Identity Provider for authentication and subsequently returned to VWO after successful authentication. 



Where supported by the account, browser, and device, the user shall be able to authenticate using a registered passkey.

The passkey authentication shall use the device/authenticator verification mechanism. 





Unauthenticated users shall not be granted access to protected VWO resources.



Invalid credentials shall not result in successful authentication.



Passwords shall not be exposed as readable text during normal password entry.



Authentication shall be performed over a secure HTTPS connection.



Authentication/session information shall not expose sensitive credentials to the user interface.



The system shall enforce configured authentication and access-control policies.



The application shall protect authentication endpoints against abusive authentication attempts according to the platform's configured security controls.



Session expiration shall require the user to authenticate again when the applicable session lifetime is exceeded. VWO documents a default two-hour inactivity expiration and an extended Remember Me duration of up to 14 days on the same browser/device. 





Given a registered VWO user And the user has valid credentials When the user enters the valid email and password And clicks Sign In Then authentication shall succeed And the user shall be redirected to the VWO account/dashboard.



Given a registered VWO user When the user enters an incorrect password And clicks Sign In Then authentication shall fail And the user shall remain unauthenticated And appropriate authentication feedback shall be displayed.



Given the login page is displayed When the user provides an invalid/unregistered email And attempts authentication Then authentication shall not succeed.



Given the login page is displayed When required login information is missing And the user attempts to sign in Then the system shall prevent successful authentication And provide appropriate validation feedback.



Given an existing VWO account When the user selects Forgot Password Then the password recovery flow shall be displayed And the user shall be able to initiate password reset using the registered email.



Given valid credentials When the user selects Remember Me and successfully signs in Then the applicable extended session behavior shall be applied on the same browser/device. 



Given an account eligible for Google authentication When the user selects Sign in with Google Then the Google authentication flow shall be initiated And successful authentication shall grant access to VWO. 



Given the organization has SSO configured When the user selects Sign in using SSO Then the user shall be redirected to the configured Identity Provider And successful authentication shall return the user to VWO. 



Given the user has a registered passkey And the browser/device supports passkeys When the user selects Sign in with Passkey Then the passkey authentication prompt shall be displayed And successful verification shall authenticate the user. 



Given the user is not authenticated When the user attempts to access a protected VWO resource Then access shall not be granted without successful authentication.





Login should provide a responsive user experience under normal operating conditions.

Authentication should support expected concurrent user traffic.

No specific response-time SLA is provided in the current requirements.

Performance SLA: Not specified.



The login experience should support:

Keyboard navigation

Accessible form controls

Accessible names/labels

Appropriate focus management

Screen-reader compatibility

Accessible validation/error messaging

Formal WCAG compliance level: Not specified.



The login functionality should operate on supported browsers and devices.

Official browser/device support matrix: Not specified in this requirement.



QA should validate at minimum:

Scenario

Expected

Invalid email

Login rejected

Invalid password

Login rejected

Empty email

Validation displayed

Empty password

Validation displayed

Both fields empty

Authentication prevented

Invalid email format

Appropriate validation

Incorrect credentials repeatedly submitted

Security controls enforced

Expired session

User required to authenticate again

Invalid password-reset request

Appropriate handling

Expired password-reset link

Reset prevented/appropriate recovery

Failed Google authentication

User remains unauthenticated

Failed SSO authentication

User remains unauthenticated

Failed Passkey authentication

User remains unauthenticated



The Jira story is complete when:

All acceptance criteria are implemented.

Functional test cases are executed.

Negative test cases are executed.

Security test coverage is completed.

Accessibility validation is completed.

Performance testing is completed against an agreed SLA.

Critical/Blocker defects are resolved.

High-severity defects are resolved or formally accepted.

Regression testing passes.

Automation coverage is implemented for applicable scenarios.

QA provides approval.



For your Playwright framework, I would subsequently create automation test IDs such as:



TC_LOGIN_002  Invalid password

TC_LOGIN_003  Invalid email

TC_LOGIN_004  Empty credentials

TC_LOGIN_005  Forgot Password navigation

TC_LOGIN_006  Remember Me

TC_LOGIN_007  Google authentication

TC_LOGIN_008  SSO authentication

TC_LOGIN_009  Passkey authentication

issues.summary: VWO Web APP https://app.vwo.com/
P1: Production login failures preventing user sign-in
issues.description:
Overview:Users are unable to sign in to the application in Production. Authentication requests are returning errors (invalid credentials) or HTTP 500 responses; some sessions hang on an indefinite spinner. This is a user-facing outage blocking access.

Actual behavior:

Valid credentials return “Invalid username or password” for multiple users.

Some users see an indefinite spinner and never reach the dashboard.

Auth endpoint intermittently returns HTTP 500 Internal Server Error.

Expected behavior:

Valid users authenticate and are redirected to their dashboard.

Invalid credentials return a clear error message prompting next steps.

Steps to reproduce:

1. Open https://app.example.com/login (or open the mobile app).2. Enter a previously working valid email/username and password.3. Click Sign In.4. Observe error (invalid credentials), spinner, or 500 response.

Environment:

Environment: Production

Platforms: Web (Chrome/Firefox/Safari) and Mobile (iOS/Android)

Affected release: latest production release (confirm build)

Impact & Severity:

Severity: Critical

Priority: P1

User impact: Production users are unable to sign in; blocks access and may impact revenue/support.

Logs / Attachments to collect:

Auth service logs, application server logs, DB logs, cache/Redis logs

Browser console logs, HAR files, screenshots

Mobile app logs

Recent deployment/change logs

Suggested immediate triage actions:

1. Check recent deployments/config changes and consider rollback if correlated.2. Review auth-service error logs and stack traces for 500s.3. Verify connectivity to user DB and session/cache stores.4. Check third-party auth/SSO provider status if applicable.5. Reproduce in staging and collect HAR + server traces.

Workaround:

No reliable workaround identified; clearing browser cookies/cache helped some users intermittently but not consistent.

Acceptance criteria for resolution:

Successful end-to-end login for affected users (web and mobile).

No 500 responses on auth endpoint for valid login attempts.

Root cause identified and fixed; monitoring stable for 24h post-fix.

Reporter: User report

Assignee: unassignedLabels: login, authentication, production, incident

Please attach logs/har/screenshot files when available and assign to the auth team for immediate investigation.
